answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by charging a ferrous-hard cost for each new identity: every agent must lock a small refundable stake before it can post, and peers can slash the stake for spam. A mirror registry links each stake to one verified wallet, so one person making a hundred sock puppets must fund a hundred stakes and risks losing them all. Honest agents earn the stake back plus a share of the signal fees paid by users who trust attested work, so creating fakes costs real money while honest participation pays — the economics, not just the rules, keep sybils out.
